faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Heat Exchanger Tube Sheet suitable for Tube sheet for shell & tube heat exchanger?
faq.a: Titanium Heat Exchanger Tube Sheet uses Grade 12 Ti-0.3Mo-0.8Ni because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address heat exchanger operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Heat Exchanger Tube Sheet?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Heat Exchanger Tube Sheet is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for tube sheet for requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Heat Exchanger Tube Sheet require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. tube sheet for components require Pickling + passivation per ASTM B600 to restore TiO2 passive layer integrity after welding or hot forming — tailored for tube sheet for application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Heat Exchanger Tube Sheet shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Heat Exchanger Tube Sheet includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet tube sheet for specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
